Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC:** Difficulty breathing after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Insect sting or bite, suspected bee or wasp, to the arm a few minutes prior to consult
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Insect sting/bite (bee vs wasp) to arm a few minutes prior to consult

History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Local reaction at sting site: slight redness, “blotchy” rash, puncture mark; no significant swelling noted by pt

• No known pet allergies; no food allergies

Assessment.content: Localized reaction to insect sting, likely bee or wasp, with mild erythema and rash at arm and no current signs of anaphylaxis on video assessment
Assessment.source_text: 1. Localized reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp) – mild erythema/rash at arm; no current signs of anaphylaxis on video assessment.

Assessment.content: Anxiety related to symptoms and concern for progression
Assessment.source_text: 2. Anxiety related to symptoms/concern for progression.

Plan_of_Care.content: Start over-the-counter antihistamine chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg, 1 tablet up to 6 times per day or a once-daily antihistamine per preference for localized insect sting reaction
Plan_of_Care.source_text:
**Localized insect sting reaction**
• Start OTC antihistamine: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg, 1 tab up to 6x/day **or** a once-daily antihistamine per preference

Plan_of_Care.content: Monitor for worsening or local infection such as spreading redness or warmth or hot area, which may need further treatment including antibiotics
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Monitor for worsening/local infection: spreading redness, warmth/hot area → may need further tx (e.g., abx)

Plan_of_Care.content: Red flag symptoms reviewed including lip swelling, difficulty breathing, and stridor
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Reviewed red flags: lip swelling, difficulty breathing, stridor

Plan_of_Care.content: If deterioration or progression occurs, patient should go straight to A&E, especially if rapid; otherwise contact clinic for appointment
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • If deterioration/progression → go straight to A&E (esp if rapid); otherwise contact clinic for appt

Plan_of_Care.content: Provide link or information on anaphylactic reactions and advise low threshold to seek help if worried
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Provide link/info on anaphylactic reactions; advised low threshold to seek help if worried

Plan_of_Care.content: No allergy testing indicated at this time
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • No allergy testing indicated at this time; consider if recurrent reactions/non-specific rashes develop

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider allergy testing if recurrent reactions or non-specific rashes develop
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • No allergy testing indicated at this time; consider if recurrent reactions/non-specific rashes develop

Follow_up_Information.content: If deterioration or progression of symptoms occurs, patient should go straight to A&E, especially if rapid; otherwise contact clinic for appointment
Follow_up_Information.source_text: • If deterioration/progression → go straight to A&E (esp if rapid); otherwise contact clinic for appt

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient advised to have a low threshold to seek help if worried about anaphylactic reactions
Follow_up_Information.source_text: • Provide link/info on anaphylactic reactions; advised low threshold to seek help if worried

Follow_up_Information.content: Allergy testing may be considered in the future if recurrent reactions or non-specific rashes develop
Follow_up_Information.source_text: • No allergy testing indicated at this time; consider if recurrent reactions/non-specific rashes develop
